sections.text: This checkpoint practices the whole unit. A recursive tree needs Box to have a known size (Box<T>). A Guard value cleans up with Drop, and with Deref it can be used where a &str is expected (Deref and Drop). Several guards share one log with Rc (Rc<T>), and the log is changed through RefCell (RefCell<T> and interior mutability). You do not write main.

The starter compiles, but four bodies are marked todo!(), a placeholder that panics with "not yet implemented" when it runs. The compiler shows warnings about unused variables until you are done. That is expected. Your Deref impl is what makes shout(&db) work in main: Rust turns the &Guard into a &String, and then into the &str that shout wants. The program prints the log at the end, so the messages show you the order in which values were created and dropped.

depth: match on tree. A Leaf has depth 1. For a Node, call depth on both children (they are Box<Tree>, and Rust lets you pass them where a &Tree is expected, as in the sum example), then give back the bigger one plus 1. Guard::new: push the message first, with log.borrow_mut().push(...), then build the Guard with Rc::clone(log). Drop: push a closed message the same way. deref: return a reference to the name field.

Signatures to match: depth(tree: &Tree) -> u32, Guard::new(name: &str, log: &Rc<RefCell<Vec<String>>>) -> Guard, Drop::drop(&mut self) and Deref::deref(&self) -> &String. The log is a Vec<String> inside a RefCell inside an Rc. Rc::strong_count in main checks that new really adds an owner. Drop order in main: drop(cache) runs early, and db is dropped at the end of its block.

exercise.prompt:
Finish the program. Four bodies are marked todo!().

(1) fn depth(tree: &Tree) -> u32: a Leaf has depth 1, and a Node has depth 1 plus the depth of its deeper child.

(2) Guard::new(name: &str, log: &Rc<RefCell<Vec<String>>>) -> Guard pushes the text opened NAME onto the log (for example opened db), and returns a Guard that holds its name and a new owner of the same log (do not copy the Vec).

(3) impl Drop for Guard pushes the text closed NAME onto the log when a Guard goes away.

(4) In impl Deref for Guard, fn deref(&self) -> &String returns a reference to the guard's name.

Do not change main. It should print:

depths: 1 2 4
owners: 3
DB
owners: 2
owners: 1
opened db
opened cache
closed cache
working
closed db
exercise.expectedOutput:
depths: 1 2 4
owners: 3
DB
owners: 2
owners: 1
opened db
opened cache
closed cache
working
closed db
hints: depth is a match on tree, and a Node asks for the depth of both children. The log is shared, so Guard::new must add an owner, not copy the Vec. new and drop both push a message onto the log.

Write to the log with log.borrow_mut().push(format!(...)). In new, push the opened message first, then build Guard { name: String::from(name), log: Rc::clone(log) }. In drop, push the closed message through self.log. deref gives back &self.name.
In depth, Tree::Leaf gives 1. For Tree::Node(left, right), write let l = depth(left); and let r = depth(right); then give back if l > r { l + 1 } else { r + 1 }.

quiz.question: Why is the variant written Node(Box<Tree>, Box<Tree>) and not Node(Tree, Tree)?
options: Without Box, a Tree would contain a Tree and have infinite size
A Box makes the tree faster to read
An enum variant cannot hold another enum

quiz.question: What does Rc::clone(&log) copy?
options: Only a pointer, and it adds 1 to the owner count
Nothing, and the owner count stays the same

quiz.question: What happens if you call log.borrow_mut() while another borrow_mut() guard on the same RefCell is still alive?
options: The second call waits until the first guard is dropped
The program panics at run time
